{{nihongo|'''Hikite Chikara no Mikoto Shrine'''|引手力命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Hikite Chikara no Mikoto Shrine''' (ひきてちからのみことじんじゃ / ひきたぢからのみことじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} at {{ill|Cape Ose|Q11437688|qid=Q11437688}} in Nishiura Enashi, {{ill|Numazu|ar|نامازو (شيزوكا)|arz|نامازو|azb|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|bg|Нумадзу|ce|Нумадзу|ceb|Numazu (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Numazu|eo|Numazu|es|Numazu (Shizuoka)|et|Numazu|fa|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|fi|Numazu|fr|Numazu|ga|Numazu|gl|Numazu|hr|Numazu|id|Numazu, Shizuoka|io|Numazu, Shizuoka|it|Numazu|ja|沼津市|ko|누마즈시|mg|Numazu|mn|Нүмазү|mzn|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|nl|Numazu|no|Numazu|pl|Numazu|pt|Numazu|ro|Numazu|ru|Нумадзу|sh|Numazu|simple|Numazu|sr|Нумазу|sv|Numazu|szl|Numazu|tg|Нумазу|th|นูมาซุ|tl|Numazu|tr|Numazu|tt|Нумадзу|uk|Нумадзу (Сідзуока)|ur|نومازو، شیزوکا|vi|Numazu, Shizuoka|war|Numazu, Shizuoka|zh|沼津市|zh_classical|沼津市|zh_min_nan|Numazu-chhī|zh_yue|沼津|qid=Q241037}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. Its former rank was shikinaisha candidate shrine (small government-offering shrine candidate) and gōsha.

=== Overview ===
It has long drawn devotion from fishing communities along {{ill|Suruga Bay|Q1201023|qid=Q1201023}}{{Sfn|Miyata|p=29}}.

The "Hikite Chikara no Mikoto Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} is often identified with this shrine, but another shrine exists in former Tagata District of {{ill|Izu Province|ar|مقاطعة إزو|be|Ідзу (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیزو|cs|Provincie Izu|cv|Идзу|de|Provinz Izu|es|Provincia de Izu|fa|ولایت ایزو|fr|Province d'Izu|gl|Provincia de Izu|hak|Yî-theu-koet|id|Provinsi Izu|it|Izu (provincia)|ja|伊豆国|ko|이즈국|lt|Idzu žemė|nl|Izu (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Izu|pt|Província de Izu|ru|Идзу (провинция)|simple|Izu Province|sk|Izu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Изу|th|แคว้นอิซุ|tr|Izu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ідзу|zh|伊豆國|zh_min_nan|Izu-kok|zh_yue|伊豆國|qid=Q860928}}: {{ill|Hikite Chikarao Shrine|Q134956261|qid=Q134956261}} (ひきたじからおじんじゃ) in Tōbosoku, {{ill|Itō, Shizuoka|ar|إتو (شيزوكا)|arz|اتو (تجمع سكان فى محافظه شيزوكا)|azb|ایتو، شیزوئوکا|ce|Ито (гӀала)|ceb|Itō|da|Itō (Shizuoka)|de|Itō (Shizuoka)|eo|Ito (Ŝizuoka)|es|Itō (Shizuoka)|et|Itō|fa|ایتو، شیزوئوکا|fi|Itō (Shizuoka)|fr|Itō|gl|Itō|he|איטו (יפן)|hu|Itó (Sizuoka)|id|Itō, Shizuoka|it|Itō|ja|伊東市|ko|이토시|lt|Itas|mzn|ایتو، شیزوئوکا|nl|Ito (Shizuoka)|pl|Itō|pt|Ito (Shizuoka)|ro|Itō (localitate)|ru|Ито (город)|sv|Ito|tg|Ито|th|อิโต|tl|Itō|tr|Itō|tt|Ито (шәһәр)|uk|Іто (Сідзуока)|ur|ایٹو، شیزوکا|vi|Itō, Shizuoka|war|Itō, Shizuoka|zh|伊東市|zh_classical|伊東市|zh_min_nan|Itô-chhī|zh_yue|伊東|qid=Q721163}} (north foot of Mt. {{ill|Mount Ōmuro (Shizuoka)|Q11434371|qid=Q11434371}}). Because no decisive historical source establishes which one corresponds to the shikinaisha "Hikite Chikara no Mikoto Shrine," the matter is unresolved. This article covers the shrine at Ōsezaki.

In {{ill|2006|Q2021|qid=Q2021}}, it was selected (under the facility name "Ōse Shrine") as one of the {{ill|100 Fishing Village Heritage Sites (Japan)|Q11519509|qid=Q11519509}}<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.gyokou.or.jp/100sen/pdf/100sijitu/si060.pdf |format=PDF |title=100 Heritage Cultural Assets of Fisheries/Fishing Villages to Preserve for the Future: Ōse Shrine|publisher=National Fisheries Port and Fishing Ground Association |accessdate=2017-08-17}}</ref>.

=== Shrine name ===
It is often called by the common name '''Ōse Shrine''' (おせじんじゃ), and this name appears on the torii plaque. It is also called '''Ōse Myōjin'''.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* '''Hikite Chikara no Mikoto''' (ひきたぢからのみこと)

Among major shrines considered shikinaisha, no others are known to enshrine a deity by this exact name. There is a theory identifying it with {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|Q849412|qid=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}} of the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}, but while Ame-no-Tajikarao is generally treated as a mountain deity, Hikite Chikara no Mikoto is a protector of the sea, so the identification is uncertain.

=== Origin and history ===
[[画像:1500year Byakushin.JPG|thumb|right|Sacred tree of the shrine<br /><small>One tree from the natural monument "Ōsezaki Byakushin Grove," estimated age 1,500 years.</small>]]
The founding period is unknown. One theory says that when a great earthquake in {{ill|Hakuhō|ja|白鳳|ru|Хакухо|zh|白鳳|qid=Q11580612}} 13 ({{ill|684|Q31128|qid=Q31128}}) suddenly uplifted the seabed by about 300 jō, creating an island called "Biwa-jima," people thought a deity had "pulled" land from {{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330}}, where much land had sunk in the same period's quakes, and began worshipping Hikite Chikara no Mikoto here. "Biwa-jima" later became tied to the mainland by sandspit formation and became {{ill|Cape Ose|Q11437688|qid=Q11437688}}.

In the late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Tametomo|de|Minamoto no Tametomo|es|Minamoto no Tametomo|fa|میناموتو نو تامه‌تومو|fr|Minamoto no Tametomo|it|Minamoto no Tametomo|ja|源為朝|ko|미나모토노 다메토모|pt|Minamoto no Tametomo|ru|Минамото-но Тамэтомо|sv|Minamoto no Tametomo|uk|Мінамото-но Таметомо|zh|源為朝|qid=Q1339356}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}}, and {{ill|Hōjō Masako|Q463961|qid=Q463961}} are said to have dedicated bows, arrows, helmet, mirror, and sword while praying for revival of the Minamoto line; after revival and establishment of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|azb|کاماکورا شوگونلوغو|be|Сёгунат Камакура|ca|Shogunat Kamakura|ckb|زنجیرە شۆگنی کاماکورا|cs|Šógunát Kamakura|de|Kamakura-Shōgunat|el|Σογκουνάτο Καμακούρα|es|Shogunato Kamakura|eu|Kamakura shogunerria|fa|شوگون‌سالاری کاماکورا|fi|Kamakura-shōgunaatti|fr|Shogunat de Kamakura|hak|Kamakura mok-fú|he|שוגונות קמקורה|hu|Kamakura-bakufu|id|Keshogunan Kamakura|it|Shogunato Kamakura|ja|鎌倉幕府|ko|가마쿠라 막부|ms|Kesyogunan Kamakura|nl|Kamakura-shogunaat|no|Kamakura-shōgunatet|pl|Kamakura (okres)|pt|Xogunato Kamakura|ru|Сёгунат Камакура|simple|Kamakura shogunate|sr|Камакура шогунат|th|รัฐบาลโชกุนคามากูระ|tr|Kamakura şogunluğu|uk|Сьоґунат Камакура|vi|Mạc phủ Kamakura|zh|镰仓幕府|zh_min_nan|Kamakura bō͘-hú|zh_yue|鎌倉幕府|qid=Q736839}}, many warriors dedicated bows and swords.

In the Nanboku-chō period, {{ill|Suzuki Shige-tomo|ja|鈴木繁伴|qid=Q17219427}}, ancestor of the Enashi Suzuki clan, ruled this area (remains thought to be his residence survive) and is said to have devoted himself to shrine rites. Repeated earthquakes and tsunamis later destroyed both residence and offerings, but as some items were found in sand, local people enshrined them and the shrine was revived over time to the present.

The precinct includes {{ill|Kamiike|ja|大瀬明神の神池|qid=Q11437694|lt=Kami-ike}}, one of the {{ill|Seven Mysteries of Izu|ja|伊豆七不思議|qid=Q11380538}}. It draws devotion as a place of purification and as a guardian deity of the sea. There is a custom of dedicating red {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=fundoshi}} for maritime safety, and a former custom of dedicating scale models of newly launched fishing boats for safe voyages and good catches. Many ema paintings of fishing scenes and wooden boat models were dedicated, and some are exhibited in the ema hall. A fire in 1892 (Meiji 25) destroyed models dedicated before then. As of 2008, some of 32 later-dedicated boats are displayed; ink inscriptions on their undersides record donor name/address/year, accurately reflecting fishing-vessel styles of Suruga Bay coasts in Meiji, Taishō, and early Shōwa, and showing the shrine's faith sphere spread widely around Suruga Bay.

=== Ōse Festival ===
[[ファイル:Cape Ose and Mount Fuji.jpg|サムネイル|300px|{{ill|Cape Ose|Q11437688|qid=Q11437688}}, site of Hikite Chikara no Mikoto Shrine]]
'''Ōse Festival''' (おせまつり) is the annual grand festival of Hikite Chikara no Mikoto Shrine, held every April 4.

On the day, neighboring communities prepare fishing boats decorated with large catch-flags and cedar/cherry twigs, and young men board in flamboyant women's dress and head to the shrine by sea. Upon reaching the cove, "fortune bales" are thrown from the boats into the sea{{Refnest|group="注釈"|Filled with pebbles and dead leaves; said to symbolize stone weights for fishing nets{{Sfn|Miyata|p=29}}.}}, then first-year crew youths dive in to retrieve them and swim ashore, carrying them straight into the shrine precinct. Stones are then picked up from the beach and attached to boats, and they return while performing a dance called "Isami-odori" on board. The shrine itself calls it a "world-famous strange festival"<ref>[http://www.osezaki.jp/osematuri.html Ōse Coastal Commercial Association / Ōse Shrine Annual Grand Festival (Ōse Festival)]</ref>, and it is considered a remnant of a community {{ill|Rite of passage|af|Deurgangsrite|ar|طقوس العبور|as|উত্তৰণৰ বিধি|az|Keçid mərasimləri|bn|উত্তরণের আচার|ca|Ritu de pas|cs|Přechodový rituál|cy|Defod newid byd|da|Overgangsrite|de|Übergangsritus|eo|Transiga rito|es|Rito de paso|et|Siirderiitus|eu|Iragate-ohikune|fa|مناسک گذار|fi|Siirtymäriitti|fr|Rite de passage|fy|Oergongsritueel|he|טקס מעבר|id|Ritus peralihan|it|Rito di passaggio|ja|通過儀礼|ko|통과 의례|la|Ritus transitorius|nl|Overgangsritueel (antropologie)|nn|Overgangsrite|no|Overgangsrite|oc|Rite de passatge|pl|Obrzęd przejścia|pt|Rito de passagem|ru|Обряды перехода|simple|Rite of passage|sv|Övergångsrit|tr|Geçiş törenleri|uk|Обряд переходу|vi|Nghi lễ trưởng thành|zh|通過儀禮|qid=Q1131696}} among fishers{{Sfn|Miyata|pp=28-29}}. It is also said to be a type of {{ill|kashima odo|Q11677163|qid=Q11677163}}.

On {{ill|April 5|Q2507|qid=Q2507}}, {{ill|1949|Q5188|qid=Q5188}} (Shōwa 24), records note that {{ill|Hirohito|Q34479|qid=Q34479}} and {{ill|Empress Nagako|Q230697|qid=Q230697}}, staying at the Numazu Imperial Villa, viewed the ceremonial big-catch dance performed on boats gathered offshore in front of the villa<ref>{{Cite book |和書 |author=Imperial Household Agency |title=Shōwa Tennō Jitsuroku Vol.10 |publisher=Tokyo Shoseki |year=2017-03-30 |page=799|isbn=978-4-487-74411-4 }}</ref>.

Today, the "Uchiura Fishing Port Festival" is also held at the same time, including seafood/local products sales and taiko performances.
